title: rubus fruticosus subsp. carpinifolius
intro: Rubus fruticosus subsp. carpinifolius, commonly known as the thimbleberry, is a subspecies of the blackberry plant that belongs to the Rosaceae family. This plant is known for its edible fruits and has been used in traditional medicine for its health benefits, including anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, and antioxidant properties. The therapeutic actions of Rubus fruticosus subsp. carpinifolius include wound healing, anti-diarrheal, and anti-cancer properties, attributed to its bioactive constituents such as ellagic acid, anthocyanins, and phenolic acids. The bioactive constituents of this plant have been shown to possess antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and anti-cancer activities, making it a potential candidate for the prevention and treatment of various diseases.
